maria.s: Hey — partner #ingest found a blob of GCS logs that include KMS ciphertexts referencing tenant=acme-corp. They're not plaintext, but we need to treat this as a potential pre-exposure. Can we sync quick on scope and whether to rotate wrapping keys?

aj: Thanks for flagging. Do we know which KMS key(s) are referenced? ciphertext example?
maria.s: Pasted sample from logs: `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/partner-keys/cryptoKeys/acme-wrap/cryptoKeyVersions/1` — appears to be partner's wrapped payloads stored in logging bucket. Not sure if any plaintext creds leaked.
samir: If it's just ciphertext (KMS+wrapped), blast radius is smaller, but we need to confirm whether any unwrapped secrets live anywhere else. First step: enumerate objects that reference that key and list owners. I can run a quick GCS filter.
len: +1 on inventory. Also want to confirm Vault integration: do we have any Transit/Vault-unwrap operations that use that key material (i.e., externalized)? Could be partner's key in their KeyRing used only for them.
sec-oncall: Recommendation: assume compromise until proven otherwise. Steps: 1) inventory (GCS objects, BigQuery exports, logs referencing key). 2) Identify consumer service accounts and last unwrap times via KMS audit logs. 3) If any unwraps were performed by our services for tenant data, schedule key rewrap/rotation and coordinate with partner.
maria.s: I started a search: `gsutil ls -r gs://partner-logs/** | xargs grep -i "acme-wrap"` — found ~42 objects in 2026-03-19..2026-03-21 range. Not sure about how many were actually decrypted.
aj: KMS audit logs query to check decrypt calls: use filter `protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricDecrypt" OR protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt"` and `resource.labels.key_ring_id="partner-keys"` and `protoPayload.request.name: "acme-wrap"`. Run in Logging Explorer.
samir: Ran query, quick summary: 6 Decrypt calls from service-account:ingest-worker@partner-prod. Two calls from redwood-analytics-sa@redwood-prod in March (likely for telemetry parsing).
len: If our analytics SA performed decrypts, we need to know what happened to the plaintext. Ask analytics for storage/processing lineage.
maria.s: Pinged analytics and partner. Partner says they rotated their application-level keys last month but didn't rotate KMS key.
sec-oncall: Proposed plan (short): - Mark key as suspected-exposed in incident tracker - Add logging alert for future decrypts on that key - Ask analytics to freeze any datasets that used decrypted payloads and snapshot for IR - Rotate (create new cryptoKey version + rewrap stored ciphertext where possible) after partner agree and after we confirm no lingering plaintext sinks.
aj: Implementation note: rotating a symmetric KMS key in GCP creates a new CryptoKeyVersion; old ciphertext can still be decrypted by old versions until you revoke. Rewrap requires decrypt+encrypt flow or use the 're-encrypt' helper. We'll need access to plaintext for rewrap unless you can do KMS rewrap with key material copy (not available in GCP).
samir: Ops task list I'm taking: 1) run full GCS blob scan for `acme-wrap` refs and export list to gs://sec-incidents/4273-acme-scan.csv 2) run Logging Explorer saved query for Decrypts and export entries 3) contact analytics prod lead for lineage and snapshot
len: Security tasks: 1) add IAM deny for non-owner principals on partner-keys (temp) 2) update Vault policy if any transit mounts use that key id 3) configure Audit log sink to forward KMS Data Access logs to sec-audit project for retention
maria.s: I'm going to open the incident ticket (INC-4273) with those steps and mark priority P2 for now. Please add any runbook steps.
sec-oncall: Quick runbook additions: - If analytics confirms they stored plaintext in internal buckets, rotate those storage-level creds immediately and do a targeted rotate of affected app secrets. - Keep partner in the loop; if they want to rotate their KMS key, provide guidance to rewrap existing ciphertexts. - If we need to rotate our own rewrapping SA keys, do an ephemeral key rotation (create new SA keypairs, reissue tokens).
aj: Small snippet to query last_decrypt time via gcloud logging (example):
```
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_cryptokey" protoPayload.methodName:Decrypt' --project=redwood-prod --freshness=30d --format='table(timestamp, protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, protoPayload.request.name)'
```

samir: FYI deploy-bot: created export `gs://sec-incidents/4273-acme-scan.csv` (preview).
deploy-bot: export job completed: 42 objects listed -> gs://sec-incidents/4273-acme-scan.csv :thumbsup:
maria.s: Ok let's try to avoid wholesale key revocation until we have partner sign-off. Meanwhile, lock down RBAC and add detection. I'll draft a short email to partner legal/sre to request timeline and whether any rewrap happened on their side.
len: Also check Vault Audit: `vault audit list` and `vault audit enable` config for transit backend. If transit mount used partner key, we need to rotate transit_key_id mapping.
aj: Noted. I can help with sample Vault commands if we have the mount path.
sec-oncall: Who's owning communication with partner? maria.s: I'll take it. Call out any internal owners in the ticket.
maria.s: Assigned owners in INC-4273: security=maria.s, ops=samir, infra=aj, analytics=rosa (cced). Will update after partner reply. :raised_hands:
len: Adding post-incident items: - validate audit retention for KMS decrypt events (90d min) - automate alert on unusual decrypt frequency per key - document runbook for cross-tenant ciphertext exposure
sec-oncall: Great. If anything escalates to P1 (active exfiltration or plaintext found in public bucket), ping immediately.
aj: One more thought — if partner wants assistance rotating, we can offer a short window to perform a coordinated rewrap and rotate. Need to schedule maintenance for analytics consumers.
maria.s: Thanks all. I'll update INC-4273 with timelines and attach the CSV export + logging query outputs when ready.
sec-oncall: Closing loop here — follow up in ticket. :lock:
